observation.visible_scene: A calm sea meeting a sandy beach at a low sun (sunset/sunrise). The bright sun sits right of center near the horizon, casting a long golden shimmer column down the water. The sky grades from blue at top to orange near the horizon with thin scattered clouds. Foreground shows wet sand with a small persistent mound/rock at lower left. The scene is otherwise static across the excerpt.
visible_changes: A single swell in the mid-distance translates shoreward (toward the bottom of the frame): in early frames the near water is only gently rippled, then a darker wave crest line builds and steepens in the mid-water, and by the later frames it breaks into a continuous band of white foam.
The broken foam advances onto the wet sand, so the foreground changes from smooth shallow water/ripples to a line of receding/running white surf by the last frames.

The sun's reflection column on the water is progressively interrupted and displaced by the moving crest and foam; in early frames it reads as one long unbroken shimmer reaching the foreground, in later frames it is broken by the wave and reappears mainly on the wet sand and churned water.

The horizon, sun position, sky/cloud pattern, and the small foreground mound stay essentially fixed, indicating the visible motion is the wave's translation and breaking rather than object motion across the beach.
outside_clip_unknowns: Whether this swell is the start of a wave set or one of many; the wave may have been forming before frame 1 and the foam may recede or be followed by another wave after the last frame.
What happens to the reflection column once the surf fully washes in or drains out.
uncertain_details: Camera motion is not clearly evidenced (horizon and sun remain fixed relative to the frame), so it is treated as essentially static with possible slight drift.
Exact wave height and the precise moment of crest break are limited by the sparse sampling; the swell and the breaking foam are interpreted as the same continuous wave.
